reading: A small multi-coloured cross pattern sits outside the big rectangles. At every single marker cell inside a rectangle, the pattern is stamped centred on the marker, and its arms are extended as full lines to that rectangle's edges; the original pattern is erased.
verb: stamp exemplar and extend its arms

slots.unit: the exemplar (multi-coloured component on the background, outside the rectangles)
slots.anchors: the single odd-coloured cells inside each rectangle
slots.arms: the exemplar's arm colour along each axis that has an arm, extended to the rectangle edge
slots.rest: exemplar erased to background; all else kept

why: every marker gets an identical exemplar copy centred on it, and each arm line spans exactly its rectangle
invariants: rectangles keep their size and position
background outside rectangles unchanged except exemplar removal

reading: The number N of 8-cells in the top row is a count. Every colour that appears exactly N times in the patterned row below the grey separator gets, in each of its columns, a bar of height N standing on the separator.
verb: draw bars for colours of count N

slots.subject: colours occurring exactly count times in the multi-coloured row
slots.bars: in each subject column, count cells of that colour directly above the separator

why: bar height equals the 8-count and only colours with that frequency are drawn

reading: The single shape is copied four times in a pinwheel: original on the left, rotated 90 degrees clockwise on top, 180 on the right, 270 at the bottom, around an empty centre square. Output side = 2*width + height of the shape.
verb: rotate four ways around a centre

slots.layout: left = unit, top = rot90 cw, right = rot180, bottom = rot270, centre empty square of the unit's height

why: output has 4-fold rotational symmetry and its left arm equals the input shape

reading: Two full horizontal and two full vertical 8-lines cut the grid into 3x3 panels. Panels are filled by position: top-middle 2, middle-left 4, centre 6, middle-right 3, bottom-middle 1; corner panels stay empty.

slots.region: the 3x3 panels cut by the separators
slots.colour: constant per panel position learned from training: T=2, L=4, C=6, R=3, B=1, corners 0

why: each non-corner panel is filled entirely with its position's colour

reading: The 3x3 input holds one shape of some colour; the output is a single cell whose colour names the shape's pattern (X -> 2, plus -> 6, the 2x2-block-plus-corner pattern -> 3, the 110/101/010 pattern -> 1), independent of the shape's colour.

slots.subject: the binary pattern of non-zero cells in the 3x3 input
slots.key: pattern -> colour lookup learned from training

why: identical patterns always give the same output colour regardless of input colour

reading: The most frequent colour in the coloured rows above the grey line is written into the centre cell of the bottom row.

slots.colour: most common colour among cells above the separator

why: exactly one cell changes, at the bottom-centre, to the majority colour of the top block

reading: The 3x3 input is scaled into a 3x3 grid of blocks: each block is a copy of the whole input where the input cell has the input's most common colour, and empty otherwise.
why: each output block is the input or empty, and copies sit exactly at cells of the input's most common colour

reading: An empty grid is filled with a 3-coloured square spiral starting along the top row and turning clockwise inwards, with one empty cell gap between turns.

slots.path: clockwise inward spiral from top-left along the top row, walls separated by one background cell

why: output is the canonical spiral for the grid size

reading: Two coloured cells at opposite ends of a row each grow toward the other until they meet; the meeting cell in the middle becomes 5.

slots.source: pairs of end cells on the same row
slots.colour: each half takes its own end colour

why: each row with two ends is filled, left half left colour, right half right colour, centre 5

reading: A two-coloured shape lies on one side of a full separator line. It is reflected across the separator with its original colours, and the original shape has its two colours swapped.

slots.copy: mirror image of the shape across the axis, original colours
slots.original: the shape kept in place with its two colours exchanged

why: reflection is the exact mirror across the separator; original cells keep shape with colours a<->b
